$comment: Mission 1.70 §25. The table exists before any overall verdict, because §25 forbids an opaque PASS without it.

fields.http_archive: a desktop Chrome string and an emulated Moto G4 mobile Chrome string
fields.note: a server may answer a declared crawler differently from a browser, and any predicate on the response inherits that

fields.common_crawl: a fetch_redirect field records the target of a redirect
fields.http_archive: the main document is the first HTML request AFTER redirects
fields.note: one route appears to record the redirect response and the other binds its main-document row to the post-redirect document, so a predicate on the response to the requested URL would not be reading the same thing
a predicate on rendered content cannot survive this; a predicate on response headers can

fields.common_crawl: IPv6 is used; reverse DNS not yet supported there

fields.http_archive: Google Cloud Platform locations based in the USA
fields.note: one vantage is stated and the other is not, so they cannot be shown equal

fields.common_crawl: a truncation reason of time implies a bound

fields.http_archive: a retry_count is recorded per test

same_world_state_family.why_plausible: Both routes capture the response headers of the main HTML document — one as raw headers inside a WARC record, the other as a structured array — so at least one non-trivial direct response property family is captured by both.
same_world_state_family.what_it_is_conditional_on: the request contract being alignable, which the table above shows is not established, with four load-bearing differences and eleven unknowns.

client_relative_propositions_are_allowed.statement: §24 permits a proposition of the form 'response property under request contract R'. It need not pretend to be a client-independent property of the server. But R must then be the SAME on both routes or explicitly equivalent, and equivalence must be documented rather than assumed.
